newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower on spillover weakness.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower on spillover weakness.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended lower on spillover bearishness from other U.S. wheat markets, traders said. Volumes were extremely light.

U.S. wheat markets drew pressure after exporters said Pakistan bought 225,000 tonnes of Australian wheat over the weekend instead of U.S. wheat. Exporters said Bangladesh likely bought 100,000 tonnes of Australian wheat over the weekend.
Wheat also saw spillover weakness from CBOT soybeans, which ended broadly lower on nearly ideal soy crop weather conditions in South America.
MGE spring wheat closed 1-1/2 to five cents lower, with March down 1-1/2 cents at $3.80. December settled two cents lower at $4.21.

Traders said LFG bought 500,000 March bushels and sold 300,000 March. Atwood/Peavey bought 400,000 March and sold 400,000 July. The Dec/March spread barely budged and was offered late at 41 cents. It closed Friday at 41-1/2 cents.
MGE barley futures ended one cent per cwt lower to five cents higher, with Dec up five cents at $6.80. March lost one cent to close at $6.62.
